title: Viniyoga of sūryaś ca

words.role: first word of the anuvāka quoted

words.meaning: thus; marks the words before it as a quotation
of the anuvāka (the section of recitation)
gāyatrī, the metre of three lines of eight syllables

words.role: with prāśane: ‘in the sipping of water’
what the mantra is used for

sandhi.rule: the visarga becomes ś before c; a + i becomes e; i before a vowel becomes y

translation.literal: Of the anuvāka “sūryaś ca”: Agni the seer, gāyatrī the metre, Sūrya the deity, the use in the sipping of water.
translation.readable: Sūryaś ca mā: seer Agni, metre gāyatrī, deity the Sun; used for sipping water.

sandhi_exceptions.note: The prayoga leaves two vowels side by side across a phrase boundary of the formula, without joining them.
The prayoga writes the visarga before the following vowel, the words left apart as separate phrases of the formula, instead of joining them.

meaning: A viniyoga is the statement said before a mantra of its seer (ṛṣi), its metre (chandas), its deity (devatā) and the use (viniyoga) it is put to. Here: the morning prāśana mantra sūryaś ca mā manyuś ca (Mahānārāyaṇa 10.32), seen by Agni and addressed to the Sun; its evening counterpart agniś ca mā is seen by Sūrya and addressed to Agni. The commas of the witness mark the pauses between the parts; a word before a comma keeps its pausal form.
in_the_rite: Morning service, step prasana, before sūryaś ca (M only).
